ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All beneficial owners, directors, managers, and authorized signatories must undergo enhanced due diligence against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT Sanctions List, Taiwan FSC domestic sanctions and watchlists, and PRC/CSRC debarment lists. PEP screening covers all current and former senior officials in China, Taiwan, and other sovereign states, plus immediate family, close associates, and sanctioned entities. Source of wealth and source of funds for any PEP must be documented. Screening must be refreshed at least every 180 days, and upon any shareholding change. Adverse media results trigger a risk rating review and potential escalation. All screening outputs must be archived for a minimum of five years and made available to the Taiwan AML reporting authority upon request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Department of Commerce Company Registration and Name Pre-Screening System (available via the MOEA Company Registration Website)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in traditional Chinese characters with an optional matching English name. The Chinese name must follow a four-tier structure: (1) a distinct section name; (2) a business title; (3) a corporate designator such as 'Limited' or 'Co., Ltd.'; and (4) an organizational type. The English name must be either a literal translation or phonetic transliteration of the Chinese name and must remain identical across all filings. Names that may confuse the public, imply obscure or unlawful business, or conflict with an existing registered name are rejected. For clinical trial CRO scope, the name must not imply medical practice absent a separate hospital or clinic license.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the MOEA rejects a proposed name, the applicant receives a written rejection notice with statutory grounds within seven working days. The applicant may file an administrative appeal within fifteen working days using the online appeal form on the MOEA portal, attaching the rejection notice, a comparative analysis of existing registered names, and a legal memorandum explaining why the proposed name is not confusing. MOEA must decide within thirty working days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit in the Taipei High Administrative Court within thirty days of receipt of the final decision, and may simultaneously submit an amended name reservation through the online portal to preserve priority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices and commercial mailboxes are not fully rejected by the Taiwan company registry for a simple limited company, but for a licensed clinical trial CRO under Taiwan FDA jurisdiction, they are rejected for all practical purposes. The Taiwan National Taxation Bureau requires an actual operational address for tax invoice issuance, records retention, and payroll. Banks providing the required bank reference letters for a CRO mandate will demand a physical inspection of the office, board meeting room, and secure data storage. The TFDA GCP inspection checklist includes an on-site verification of facilities. Therefore a physical office lease (minimum 20 square meters, with a dedicated compliance manager) is mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (a) submit registered office address and lease to MOEA; (b) tax authority will conduct an unannounced address verification within 90 days of registration; (c) bank account opening includes visit by a bank officer; (d) TFDA may perform a risk-based on-site inspection before issuing the CRO license; (e) annual inspection by the municipal health department is likely. Quantified risk: High — 65-75% probability of at least one unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of operation, rising to approximately 90% following the issuance of the clinical trial CRO license.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act of the Republic of China (Taiwan), as amended; applicable sections include Articles 1-2 and 6 (company definition and registration), 128-139 (promoters and share subscription), 154 and 156 (share capital and flexible capital rules), 172 and 181-193 (board meetings, directors, and chairmanship), 216 (statutory officers), and 419-420 (incorporation application and filing). Supplemented by the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Articles 4 and 12, and the MOEA Regulations on Company Registration Application and Review Matters.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs, Company Registration Division; with the Investment Commission of MOEA as the competent authority for foreign investment approval before company registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application Form for establishment of a company limited by shares, together with the registered Articles of Incorporation filed through the MOEA Company and Commercial Registration System.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Companies Act; no statutory minimum paid-in capital and no blocked escrow account is generally required. However, all issued shares must be subscribed and paid in through a domestic corporate bank account, verified by a Taiwan-licensed certified public accountant issuing a capital verification report. Foreign-invested capital must be remitted into Taiwan with an approved foreign investment permission letter and a bank remittance certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION NO. FBR/2025/001 OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN JV LIMITED (the Company) HELD IN TAIPEI, TAIWAN ON THE EFFECTIVE DATE UNANIMOUSLY ADOPTED BY THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS.

WHEREAS, the Company is being formed as a company limited by shares under the Companies Act of the Republic of China for the purpose of conducting multinational clinical trial contract research organization (CRO) management; and

WHEREAS, the shareholders have agreed on the authorized share capital and paid-in capital of the Company and have subscribed for all issued shares to be conducted in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation and the capital verification report of a certified public accountant; and

WHEREAS, Articles 6 and 420 of the Companies Act require a formal registration application with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and the establishment of the Company's statutory governance bodies before commencing business; and

WHEREAS, the Board of Directors is required to authorize the corporate filing, banking, appointment of officers, and registered office.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, ADOPTED AND APPROVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. ADOPTION OF REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office of the Company shall be at [address in Taiwan], which is adopted as the statutory domicile and principal place of business of the Company. The Company Secretary or registered agent manager is directed to execute all lease, utility, and mailing agreements.

2. SHARE CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION: The authorized share capital of the Company is as set out in the Articles. All shares are subscribed and shall be fully paid in cash to the corporate bank account of the Company. The management is directed to deposit the subscription amounts and to obtain the bank certificate and CPA capital verification report required for registration.

3. APPOINTMENT OF OFFICERS: The following individuals are appointed as statutory officers of the Company: (a) the chairman of the board; (b) the general manager and principal representative in Taiwan; (c) the company secretary; (d) the chief financial officer; and (e) the money laundering compliance and data protection officer. The officers shall act within the authority granted by the Articles and applicable law.

4. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Company shall open corporate bank accounts with one or more licensed banks in Taiwan. The chairman, general manager, and chief financial officer, or any two of them jointly, shall be the authorized signatories. The bank mandates and signing instructions are expressly approved.

5. GOVERNANCE AND FILING: The Company Secretary and general manager are directed to prepare, execute, and submit the Company Registration Application, tax registration, foreign investment registration, and clinical trial CRO licensing documents to all relevant authorities and to represent the Company in all governmental procedures.

6. EFFECTIVENESS: This resolution may be executed in multiple counterparts and takes effect immediately. This resolution shall remain in force until amended or rescinded by a subsequent board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Foreign Investment Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Company and Commercial Registration Central Information System; Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) of Taiwan.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the MOEA Company and Commercial Registration Central Information System and complete the company name pre-reservation form for both the English and Chinese names. Simultaneously file with the Investment Commission, MOEA, an application for investment approval under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, specifying the proposed joint-venture equity structure, paid-in capital, shareholder identities, and the clinical trial CRO management business scope. The application must include a board pre-approval memorandum, audited group annual reports or financial statements, and proof of compliance with AML rules. Approved name reservation is valid for six months. If the proposed name is similar to an existing registered company, the system will issue a rejection requiring one or more alternate names. If foreign investment approval is placed under review, supply beneficial ownership declarations and bank reference letters within 14 days.
required_dossiers: MOEA company name reservation application form
Certified translation of English and Chinese company names
Foreign investment application form and schedule of shareholders
Proposed Articles of Incorporation
Sino-foreign joint venture agreement
Board resolution or consent of parent companies
Shareholder passport/ID and beneficial ownership declaration
Power of attorney for local agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File an amended name reservation with alternate names on the same portal, or submit supplementary beneficial ownership and source-of-funds documents to the Investment Commission within 14 days. If the foreign investment application is denied, submit a written appeal to the Investment Commission within 30 days under the Administrative Appeal Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription, Bank Deposit, and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Taiwanese bank for corporate account and capital deposit; Taiwan-licensed certified public accountant for capital verification report; Taiwan notary public for execution authentication.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the name reservation and foreign investment approval, the promoters shall execute the Articles of Incorporation and subscribe all ordinary shares. Open a domestic corporate NT dollar bank account in the name of the proposed company through a licensed Taiwanese bank, deposit the subscribed capital, and obtain a bank deposit certificate. A Taiwan-licensed certified public accountant must then audit the capital contribution and issue the CPA capital verification report. If foreign shareholders remit capital from abroad, the remittance certificate and foreign exchange declaration must be retained. All shareholder consent forms and board appointment statements must be signed and notarized before a Taiwan notary public, or, where permitted, notarized by the representative office of the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office if executed abroad. The minimum paid-in capital requirement is none, but capital sufficiency for the operational scope must be supported by a cash-flow projection.
required_dossiers: Executed Articles of Incorporation
Bank deposit certificate from the domestic corporate account
CPA capital verification report
Bank remittance certificate for inbound foreign invested capital
Share subscription schedule and shareholders' consent letters
Notarized signature page or notarial oath as applicable
Foreign investment approval letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or CPA rejects the verification, correct the share subscription table, refloat capital deposit instructions, or obtain a fresh bank confirmation. Re-execute notarized signatures and resubmit within 7 business days. If notarization is challenged abroad, obtain an apostille or Taiwan consular legalization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs, Company Registration Division; online through the MOEA Company Registration System.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation as a company limited by shares through the MOEA Company Registration Online Portal. Submit the application under Companies Act Articles 6 and 419, using the statutory Company Registration Application Form. Attach the notarized Articles, CPA capital verification report, bank certificate, foreign investment approval letter, directors' appointment letters and written consents, identification documents of directors and shareholders, and proof of the registered office lease. The examiner will verify the corporate name, lawful business purpose, capital adequacy, and governance documentation. After approval, the MOEA issues the Company Registration Certificate and assigns the unified business number. Should the examiner issue a correction notice, the applicant must cure all deficiencies within 15 days or the application will be suspended; an administrative remedy is available by filing a petition with the MOEA within 30 days of suspension.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Application Form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
CPA capital verification report
Bank deposit certificate
Foreign investment approval letter from the Investment Commission
Directors' appointment letters and written consents
Director and shareholder identification documents
Registered office lease or certificate of address
Company seal specimen and authorized signatory list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the MOEA correction notice within 15 days by uploading the missing documents or amending the Articles. If the application is suspended, file a formal administrative petition to MOEA within 30 days and, if necessary, advance to the Taipei High Administrative Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Uniform Invoice Number, and Statutory Employer Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Finance, National Taxation Administration, local branch office in Taiwan; Labor and Health Insurance administration if hiring.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the MOEA Company Registration Certificate, file the establishment tax registration with the local branch of the National Taxation Administration, Ministry of Finance. Submit the company registration certificate, Articles, office lease or certificate of registered address, legal representative ID, and seal card. Complete the Uniform Invoice Number assignment, request authority to issue uniform invoices if taxable sales will exceed the threshold, and register the employer for labor and health insurance. The tax authority will confirm the date of business commencement and, if relevant, VAT and profit-seeking enterprise income tax status. If the tax authority raises deficiencies or requests a field inspection, the company should submit the amended documents or make the office available for inspection within 10 days. Failure to cure may result in provisional suspension of uniform invoice issuance.
required_dossiers: MOEA Company Registration Certificate
Articles of Incorporation
Tax registration application form of the National Taxation Administration
Registered office lease or utility bill
Legal representative passport and resident certificate
Company seal card and signature specimen
Uniform invoice usage application
Bank account confirmation for tax payments
Labor and health insurance registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit correction documents through the online tax filing portal within 10 days. If the tax office issues a provisional suspension of uniform invoice issuance, appeal to the local branch and provide evidence of the corrected registration within 20 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: TFDA Clinical Trial CRO Registration and GCP Compliance Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan Food and Drug Administration (TFDA), Clinical Trials Division, Ministry of Health and Welfare; and institutional review boards (IRB) for each clinical trial.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the Taiwan Food and Drug Administration (TFDA) of the Ministry of Health and Welfare for the CRO clinical trial registration and GCP compliance authorization. For each multinational drug trial, the sponsor or the appointed CRO must also file the Clinical Trial Application and obtain IRB/ethics committee approval before participants are enrolled. The TFDA registration dossier must establish the responsible legal entity in Taiwan, designate qualified trial coordinators, provide detailed SOPs for protocol management, data integrity, adverse event reporting, pharmacovigilance, and record retention in Chinese. Commercial general liability and clinical trial insurance are mandatory. The TFDA may inspect the offices, computer systems, and subcontractor agreements under GCP audit standards. If the application is queried, respond to the administrative deficiency letter within 30 days; a rejection can be appealed to the Ministry of Health and Welfare.
required_dossiers: TFDA CRO registration application form
MOEA Company Registration Certificate
Commercial liability insurance and clinical trial insurance certificates
Detailed GCP standard operating procedures
Qualification and CVs of trial coordinators and responsible medical officer
Medical doctor license of the named trial physician
Sponsor authorization and contract for clinical trial management
Data integrity, pharmacovigilance, and record retention policies
IRB approval or clinical trial approval for each trial
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit a supplementary document within the strict 30-day deficiency period. If the TFDA denies the application, file an administrative appeal to the Ministry of Health and Welfare within 30 days of formal denial, followed by administrative litigation if necessary.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Taiwan Food and Drug Administration (TFDA), Ministry of Health and Welfare; supplemented by MOEA Industrial Development Administration for company service-sector registration and local municipal labor inspection for occupational safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Human Clinical Trial Contract Research Organization (CRO) GCP Compliance Authorization and TFDA Clinical Trial Management Registration (non-manufacturing, professional services license).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (MOENV), Taiwan, successor to the Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable / Exempt for pure clinical trial CRO management; no EIA Full Report or Initial Environmental Examination is required because the business does not engage in physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing. If the company later adds a clinical specimen repository or central laboratory, the operator must file an environmental self-monitoring listing with MOENV and may be required to perform an Initial Environmental Examination.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial wastewater discharge from CRO management services; no process VOC emissions or hazardous waste generation in the ordinary course. Office wastewater entering a municipal sewer must meet local sewer ordinance parameters, generally pH 6.0-9.0, suspended solids not exceeding 300 mg/L, and BOD not exceeding 300 mg/L. Any ancillary biological specimen storage must comply with biological waste disposal rules and the Medical Waste Regulation, with hazardous biological waste incinerated or treated by a licensed medical waste disposal facility.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for a pure office-based clinical trial CRO; no Civil Defense fire permit is required for hazardous chemical storage because no dangerous substances are stored. A standard commercial office must nevertheless pass the local Fire Bureau fire safety inspection if the usable area exceeds the regulatory threshold or if the building certificate requires a fire safety management plan. The company must also certify occupational safety under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including office lighting, ergonomics, first aid, and emergency evacuation plans. If laboratory or biological specimen handling is added, obtain occupational health clearance from the local labor inspection office and bacterial/biohazard containment approval from MOENV.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (National Taxation Administration) and the local Regional National Taxation Bureau with jurisdiction over the registered place of business; online electronic portal: Ministry of Finance E-tax Portal (tax.nat.gov.tw); related export/customs registration is administered by the Directorate General of Customs, Taiwan; electronic invoice data is handled through the Electronic Invoice Integration Service Platform (einvoice.nat.gov.tw).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Because the CN_JV_LTD is a China-domiciled equity joint venture, it is treated in the Taiwan jurisdiction as a non-resident foreign juridical entity. The procurement procedure is as follows: (1) Obtain prior approval from the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs before establishing any Taiwan branch or acquiring a Taiwan profit-earning presence; if the investor is mainland-controlled, additional cross-strait investment screening applies. (2) Complete branch or representative office registration with the Department of Commerce of the Ministry of Economic Affairs and obtain the Taiwan branch registration certificate; designate a resident tax representative and appoint a local responsible person. (3) File the tax registration application with the competent Regional National Taxation Bureau for profit-seeking enterprise and business tax registration, attaching the foreign company certificate of incorporation, branch registration certificate, lease or ownership evidence for the fixed place of business, bank proof, responsible person identification, and authorization of the tax representative. (4) Receive the eight-digit Unified Business Number (UBI) and trade-tax registration authentication from the National Taxation Bureau; for a non-resident seller with no fixed place of business, apply for non-resident business tax registration once annual Taiwan-source taxable revenue exceeds the statutory New Taiwan Dollar threshold. (5) Activate the Ministry of Finance E-tax Portal account using the responsible person's digital certificate, register for electronic Uniform Invoice service if invoices are to be issued, and, where physical clinical trial materials are exported, obtain a Taiwan Customs Registrar Code for export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The Taiwan branch or permanent establishment is taxed at the entity level under the Income Tax Act for profit-seeking enterprises on Taiwan-source income at the prevailing corporate rate, and there is no tax transparency, pass-through, or disregarded-entity treatment for a branch of a foreign equity joint venture. For business tax/VAT purposes, the Taiwan branch is a distinct VAT taxpayer obligated to charge Business Tax on taxable sales and to file periodic Business Tax returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan tax legislation does not provide check-the-box or hybrid entity elections analogous to the United States rules. A foreign corporation cannot elect partnership, transparency, or disregarded-entity treatment for Taiwan tax purposes; classification follows actual incorporation and permanent-establishment principles.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Business Tax under the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for a Taiwan resident or branch entity; tax registration is mandatory before taxable business activity commences. For non-resident businesses supplying cross-border electronic services or offshore trade into Taiwan, mandatory registration applies when annual Taiwan-source taxable turnover exceeds NT$480,000 (New Taiwan Dollars).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: A VAT-registered Taiwan business must issue Uniform Invoices for taxable sales. Where electronic Uniform Invoices are used, the taxpayer connects to the Ministry of Finance Electronic Invoice Integration Service Platform through a certified turnkey/API channel and transmits invoice data within 48 hours of issuance, storing the cloud invoice record in the central platform. Taiwan does not impose a real-time per-transaction government pre-clearance or digital-stamping protocol, but the platform validates allocation codes, sequential numbering, and data integrity, and automatic audit matching reconciles B2B and B2C invoices against the Business Tax return.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the zero-rating provisions of the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act, zero rating is available where: (a) physical goods are genuinely exported from Taiwan under a Customs export declaration; (b) services are rendered in Taiwan to an offshore customer and are actually used or consumed outside Taiwan, with no direct enjoyment or consumption in Taiwan; and (c) services are directly connected with international transportation. For a Contract Research Organization serving foreign pharmaceutical sponsors, qualifying zero-rated services may include central protocol design, regulatory dossier preparation, central data management, biostatistics, medical writing, and pharmacovigilance delivered to an offshore sponsor where the benefit is realized outside Taiwan. Services tied to Taiwanese trial sites, subject-facing activities, local regulatory filings with the Taiwan Food and Drug Administration, or warehousing of investigational products in Taiwan are generally treated as used in Taiwan and remain subject to 5% Business Tax. The zero rate must be substantiated by contract, invoice, foreign exchange receipt, and evidence of offshore use.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration issued by Taiwan Customs in the exporter's name for any exported clinical supplies, biological specimens, investigational drugs, or trial-related goods
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing Taiwan as origin and the foreign sponsor or offshore consignee as destination

Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Foreign Exchange Income Certificate issued by an authorized Taiwan bank evidencing receipt of the contract consideration from the foreign sponsor through SWIFT or wire transfer
Executed clinical trial master service agreement and work orders identifying the offshore sponsor, trial sites, and precise scope of CRO services
Commercial invoices, milestone invoices, and service completion certificates signed by the foreign client
Zero-rated sales list and electronic Uniform Invoice records showing the 0% tax code
Certificate of actual offshore consumption, sworn declaration from the foreign recipient, and any Taiwan trial authority or ethics committee approvals needed to demonstrate the place of use
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: On audit, the tax authority will require all export documentation, evidence of actual physical exit for goods, offshore use for services, and proof of foreign exchange repatriation within the statutory period. If zero-rating is disallowed because documents are missing, inconsistent, or fraudulent, the transaction is recharacterized as a domestic taxable sale at 5%, the underpaid Business Tax is assessed with overdue interest, and penalty provisions of the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act permit fines of one to five times the underpaid tax. Fabricated Customs declarations, false FIRCs, or fictitious offshore contracts may also trigger criminal investigation under the Tax Collection Act and the Customs Anti-Smuggling Act, with imprisonment and fines, and any input VAT previously refunded in respect of the zero-rated transaction is clawed back together with penalties. Repeated non-compliance can lead to suspension of electronic Uniform Invoice privileges and mandatory audit scrutiny of all future zero-rating claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC); the Ministry of Economic Affairs' Investment Commission administers relevant foreign-investment approvals, and the Financial Supervisory Commission regulates banks. The payload identifies China as the sovereign country but Taiwan as the jurisdiction. This dossier treats Taiwan as the place of incorporation and banking; it does not establish that a PRC-incorporated JV may invest in or operate in Taiwan.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Taiwan dollar is convertible for ordinary current-account transactions through authorized foreign-exchange banks. Taiwan does not generally require conversion of foreign-currency receipts into NTD or impose a general profit-remittance restriction. Capital-account transactions, foreign investment, securities transactions, and large or otherwise regulated foreign-exchange settlements remain subject to applicable reporting, approval, and documentation requirements. A Taiwan company generally must support dividend remittances with corporate approvals, financial statements, tax-payment evidence, and bank-required documentation. Foreign-exchange settlement declarations and annual limits apply; transactions exceeding applicable limits or requiring prior approval must be referred to the bank and, where required, the CBC. The precise limits and process must be confirmed against current CBC rules and the company's transaction classification before execution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Taiwan generally has no mandatory export-proceeds surrender ratio or general statutory deadline requiring exporters to convert receipts into NTD. Export proceeds may generally be retained in foreign-currency accounts, subject to bank KYC, transaction-purpose evidence, applicable foreign-exchange reporting, and tax and accounting requirements. The bank may request contracts, invoices, shipping or service-delivery evidence, and export declarations where applicable. This conclusion is for Taiwan and must not be applied to mainland China, where separate foreign-exchange and export-proceeds rules may apply.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a substitute for a Taiwanese corporate bank account. Taiwan does not provide a general passport allowing an offshore electronic-money institution to conduct regulated domestic banking or foreign-exchange settlement without required local authorization. An offshore EMI may be considered for limited payment services only after confirming its licensing status, Taiwan cross-border service restrictions, permitted funding and withdrawal flows, foreign-exchange reporting treatment, and the receiving bank's acceptance. It should not be used to receive registered capital, bypass investment controls, or avoid bank KYC.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No universal rule requires every director to appear physically for corporate account opening. Banks set their own risk-based procedures and may require an in-person interview, notarized or legalized documents, local representative attendance, or enhanced verification. Remote onboarding is not assured, particularly for a foreign-invested company, non-resident beneficial owners, complex ownership, or PRC-linked funding. Confirm requirements with each bank before submitting originals or initiating transfers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the stated China sovereign-country field and Taiwan jurisdiction, or uncertainty whether the applicant is Taiwan-incorporated or PRC-incorporated.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the Taiwan company registration certificate, articles, registered address, tax registration, ownership chart, constitutional documents, and a written explanation of the entity's legal place of incorporation. If the applicant is PRC-incorporated or PRC-controlled, provide Taiwan legal advice and evidence of any required cross-strait investment approvals before account opening or funding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PRC-origin capital, PRC beneficial ownership, or a proposed investment, loan, service, or payment that may be subject to Taiwan cross-strait restrictions or approval.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide ultimate beneficial ownership records, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence, board and shareholder approvals, investment registration or approval documents, transaction agreements, and bank-ready evidence of the remitting party and payment purpose. Obtain Taiwan regulatory advice on applicable cross-strait restrictions; do not represent that an ordinary foreign-investment approval resolves separate cross-strait requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Clinical-trial CRO receipts or payments involving sponsors, sites, investigators, vendors, or patients in multiple jurisdictions, particularly where payment descriptions do not match contracts or invoices.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide sponsor and vendor contracts, statements of work, invoices, trial or project identifiers, evidence of milestone completion, counterparty identification, payment schedules, and documentation establishing the lawful commercial purpose. Maintain appropriate confidentiality controls for clinical and personal data.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large, unusual, circular, third-party, or split foreign-exchange transfers, including settlement volumes inconsistent with the company's declared business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide transaction-level contracts and invoices, shipping or service-delivery evidence, bank statements tracing funds to the originating account, board approvals where relevant, accounting entries, tax records, and the applicable foreign-exchange declaration or approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed person, adverse-media, or high-risk-jurisdiction matches involving shareholders, directors, sponsors, sites, or payment intermediaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide identity and beneficial-ownership records, screening results, explanation and resolution of name matches, counterparty risk assessment, underlying contract and payment purpose, and any required licenses or approvals. Do not process a transaction pending resolution of a confirmed restriction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Before funding, confirm that the Taiwan entity is legally established, that the investor and investment route are permitted, and that all required investment registration, approval, or cross-strait filings are complete. Obtain the receiving bank's written instructions on account type, remitter-name matching, currency, beneficiary details, foreign-exchange declaration, and supporting documents. Route funds by SWIFT from an account in the registered investor's name; identify the payment as paid-in capital only where it is legally subscribed and properly registered, and use the bank's prescribed purpose classification rather than an invented code. Provide subscription or capital-increase documents, shareholder and board resolutions, investment approval or registration evidence, ownership chart, source-of-funds records, and remittance advice. Do not route capital through an unrelated affiliate, personal account, offshore EMI, or intercompany account to avoid review. Retain bank credit advice and accounting and registration evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use an authorized Taiwan bank for SWIFT MT103 transfers and foreign-exchange settlement. Match each payment to the CRO service contract, invoice, project milestone, recipient, and any required tax withholding or reporting. For documentary trade or larger contractual obligations, use a commercial letter of credit, documentary collection, or bank guarantee where commercially appropriate and available; CRO services are commonly settled by wire against contractual milestones rather than an LC. Reconcile beneficiary, currency, purpose, and supporting evidence before release. Dividend or other profit remittances require valid corporate authorization and satisfaction of applicable tax, accounting, investment, and bank documentation requirements. Apply the payer bank's current screening and reporting rules and preserve transaction records.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized bank, supported by an identifiable underlying exposure and subject to bank eligibility, documentation, and applicable reporting requirements.
Foreign-exchange swaps with an authorized bank for documented liquidity or hedging needs, subject to counterparty limits and regulatory requirements.
Currency swaps with an authorized bank where suitable for the entity's actual exposure, subject to transaction documentation, accounting treatment, and applicable reporting.

Non-deliverable forwards only where the relevant currency, product, counterparty, and transaction are permitted and the authorized bank confirms the applicable Taiwan regulatory and settlement treatment; do not assume unrestricted availability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) filing (實質受益人申報) with controlling shareholder and senior management details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MOEA Company Registration & Information System (national commercial registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 each year; changes in beneficial ownership, including any transfer of Taiwan JV equity by the Chinese parent or its shareholders, must be re-filed within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: NT$50,000–NT$500,000 fine per violation (Company Act §22-1); fines re-imposed cumulatively for each continued default notification cycle; company and responsible officers jointly liable; material refusal may trigger administrative dissolution under Company Act §10

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual profit-seeking enterprise income tax return (營利事業所得稅結算申報) with tax reconciliation schedules and CPA-attested financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (jurisdiction of the registered office; e-filing portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May 31 for calendar-year accounting periods; one-month extension available when an accredited tax agent handles the filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 10% of assessed tax (minimum NT$1,500, capped at NT$30,000); demand-notice default raises surcharge to 20% (minimum NT$3,000, capped at NT$90,000); late-payment penalty of 1% per 2 days up to 15% plus postal-bank interest; understated or hidden milestone revenue subject to penalty up to 2x–3x of evaded tax

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Convene Annual General Meeting and obtain shareholder ratification of the annual business report, financial statements, and profit appropriation / loss-offset proposal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting; approved records entered in the statutory minute book and retained for inspection by MOEA upon audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year JV: on or before June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible officers fined NT$10,000–NT$50,000 for violating the AGM deadline (Company Act §170); repeated failure combined with other statutory non-filings may trigger MOEA administrative dissolution order (Company Act §10)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual final-accounts filing (公司決算書表) for CPA-audit-mandated companies; audited balance sheet, income statement, cash-flow statement, and equity-change statement bearing the CPA's audit report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MOEA Central Company Registration Office; certified copy also attached to the local tax bureau's annual return file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Lodged with MOEA in the AGM approval cycle, no later than June 30; CPA report must be dated on or before the AGM date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Officers fined NT$10,000–NT$50,000 for failure to file (Company Act §20); non-CPA-certified filing treated as non-filing, exposing the JV to Income Tax Act reassessment and understatement penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual clinical-trial CRO license / TFDA registration renewal and GCP compliance declaration for trial-management services
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Taiwan Food and Drug Administration (TFDA), Ministry of Health and Welfare
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal application no later than 60 days before license expiry; GCP and pharmacovigilance records maintained on a rolling annual calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or failed renewal suspends authority to manage clinical trials; unlicensed operation is subject to Administrative Penalties Act fines and immediate suspension of trial services until re-registration

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory CPA audit when paid-in capital reaches NT$30 million or annual net sales reach NT$50 million (MOEA 'Company Final-Accounts Filing and Audit Measures' under Company Act §20); public companies and banking/insurance/securities/financial institutions are always audited. A clinical-trial CRO invoicing milestone-based USD payments will normally cross the revenue threshold and must budget for a full CPA audit; below threshold, a CPA review may be elected for lender or sponsor due-diligence comfort.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan-IFRS for public companies; Business Enterprises Financial Accounting Standards (BEAS, IFRS-for-SME-aligned) for non-public companies; books kept in New Taiwan Dollars under the Business Accounting Act; USD-denominated milestone contracts translated at SITE-announced foreign-exchange rates with revenue recognition per milestone completion evidence.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Company Act §22-1, the JV must annually re-file its register of ultimate beneficial owners (natural persons) with MOEA by March 31. Any shareholding transfer, including a restructuring at the Chinese parent level that changes control of the Taiwan JV, triggers a 30-day re-filing. The registered office must hold signed UBO declarations with passport/ID copies updated annually; both Taiwanese contributing shareholders and the PRC parent's ultimate shareholders must be traced to natural persons, and nominee arrangements are disregarded by the authority. Dividends flowing to the Chinese parent must be matched against the beneficial owner register for tax-withholding consistency.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Shareholders' Meeting Minute Book (股東會議事錄) and Board Minute Book (董事會議事錄)
Register of Ultimate / Practical Beneficial Owners (實質受益人資料)
Company seal and chop register (印鑑/印章留存簿)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$900–US$2,600 per year (Taipei/Taichung corporate-service provider: registered office address, local company secretary, AGM minute preparation, and UBO filing handling)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,500–US$8,500 (full CPA annual audit and final-accounts certification; low end applies when net sales remain below NT$50 million and a review-only report is elected)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% corporate income tax on taxable income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Taiwan generally has no broad corporate tax holiday for ordinary clinical-trial CRO activities. Potential incentives may include the Statute for Industrial Innovation, qualifying research and development credits, and selected investment or biotechnology incentives. Eligibility requires statutory qualification, documentary substantiation, timely election, and compliance with sector-specific approval conditions. Dividends distributed by a Taiwan company to a nonresident shareholder are generally subject to 21% withholding tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (營利事業所得稅結算申報書), filed electronically through the Taiwan Ministry of Finance e-filing system administered by the National Taxation Bureau. Supporting schedules include the income statement, balance sheet, tax reconciliation, fixed-asset schedules, related-party transaction disclosures, and transfer-pricing documentation where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; a provisional income tax return may also be required for eligible companies.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year taxpayer, annual filing and payment are generally due by May 31 of the following year. A taxpayer using a non-calendar fiscal year generally files within five months after fiscal year-end. Provisional income tax filing and payment are generally due during September for the first six months of the current fiscal year, subject to statutory eligibility and exceptions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unified business number, legal name, registered address, tax office, accounting period, paid-in capital, industry classification, and legal representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Taiwan entity's own unified business number. Do not report the foreign parent as the taxpayer unless the filing concerns a Taiwan permanent establishment or withholding obligation of the foreign enterprise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book revenue, cost of services, operating expenses, non-operating income, non-operating expenses, and net accounting profit or loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include revenue from CRO management, clinical-trial coordination, data management, monitoring, regulatory support, and other services performed or economically attributable to the Taiwan entity. Separate pass-through clinical-trial costs from service revenue where legally and economically supportable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs for nondeductible expenses and exclusions for non-taxable or separately taxed income; deductions for allowable expenses, depreciation, amortization, and statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile Taiwan-booked results to Taiwan taxable income. Foreign taxes, shareholder expenses, unsupported management fees, excessive related-party charges, fines, penalties, and undocumented expenses may be denied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of related parties, transaction categories, amounts, pricing methods, payment terms, and cross-border transaction data.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose transactions with the mainland Chinese parent, affiliates, foreign sponsors, laboratories, contract sites, data providers, and other controlled parties when the statutory related-party definition is met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Arm's-length adjustment, tested-party information, selected method, comparable analysis, and effect on taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Document the functions, assets, and risks of the Taiwan JV, including sponsor contracting, investigator-site management, quality control, pharmacovigilance coordination, regulatory interface, data handling, and clinical-trial risk allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year assessed losses claimed against current-year taxable income, subject to statutory eligibility and filing requirements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only losses formally recognized by the Taiwan tax authority and supported by compliant books, records, and required filings. A change in ownership or business activity may affect eligibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying R&D credits, investment credits, withholding credits, and other statutory credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain project-level evidence for qualifying R&D, personnel, subcontractor, laboratory, software, and trial-development expenditure. Do not claim credits merely because the activity is pharmaceutical or clinical in nature.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income, applicable rate, gross tax, credits, tax paid, withholding credits, balance payable, and refund position.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile corporate tax with provisional payments, withholding certificates, and any foreign tax credit claims. Payment must be made by the filing deadline even if electronic filing is completed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial statements, tax reconciliation schedules, audit or accountant certification where required, transfer-pricing reports, and incentive evidence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain English and Chinese versions of material intercompany agreements, invoices, allocation keys, board approvals, trial budgets, and evidence of actual services.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing may result in statutory late-filing or non-filing surcharges, generally calculated by reference to tax payable and subject to statutory minimums and caps. Tax assessed after non-filing may be determined by the tax authority. Underreported tax is subject to additional tax, interest, and possible penalties. Delayed payment generally attracts daily interest or surcharge under the Tax Collection Act. Intentional evasion may trigger criminal liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Provisional Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return, filed through the Ministry of Finance electronic filing platform where the company is subject to provisional filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally filed and paid in September for the first six months of the current fiscal year, subject to statutory exemptions, approved accounting-period rules, and qualification conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation based on the preceding year's assessed tax or the current-period accounting results, depending on the permitted method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Taiwan entity's prior-year assessed tax or current-period results only. Do not use the foreign shareholder's consolidated tax data.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: First-half revenue, expenses, accounting profit, tax adjustments, and provisional taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the same related-party pricing and expense substantiation standards used for the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisional tax payable, prior credits, and payment amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain proof of payment and reconcile the provisional amount in the annual return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or pay may result in surcharge, interest, assessment based on available information, and later annual-return adjustments. A provisional filing does not replace the annual corporate income tax return.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on dividends distributed by a Taiwan company to a nonresident individual, foreign company, or other nonresident recipient, subject to applicable statutory exemptions or treaty relief. Dividends to Taiwan-resident corporate shareholders are governed by separate domestic rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient, verify the relevant Taiwan tax treaty or applicable cross-border arrangement, confirm beneficial ownership and limitation conditions, and prepare the prescribed application or exemption documentation. The Taiwan payer generally must withhold at the domestic rate unless the reduced rate or exemption is properly supported and administratively available. Where advance approval is required, submit the application to the competent National Taxation Bureau before payment. Keep the certificate, treaty analysis, ownership chart, board resolution, dividend voucher, and payment records. Taiwan and mainland China should not be treated as covered by an ordinary bilateral comprehensive income tax treaty without confirming the currently effective legal instrument and administrative practice; absent confirmed relief, apply the domestic rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to a nonresident are generally subject to 20% withholding tax. Interest paid to a nonresident is generally subject to 20%, with certain qualifying interest categories, including specified securities or financial instruments, potentially subject to 15%. Treaty rates may reduce these rates if the recipient qualifies, beneficial ownership is established, residence documentation is valid, and required procedures are completed. Payments for software, databases, clinical-trial know-how, regulatory materials, or technical support must be classified by substance rather than label. Service fees may also attract 20% withholding where Taiwan-source income rules apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File generally required where annual Taiwan revenue is at least NTD 300 million or annual cross-border controlled transactions reach at least NTD 200 million, subject to statutory exclusions and simplified documentation rules. Master File generally applies where the multinational group's consolidated revenue reaches at least NTD 7 billion and the Taiwan entity meets the applicable cross-border related-party conditions. Country-by-Country reporting may apply to an ultimate parent or surrogate parent with group consolidated revenue meeting the statutory threshold, commonly NTD 27 billion or the prescribed equivalent threshold.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other methods permitted under Taiwan transfer-pricing regulations where the standard methods cannot reliably be applied and the selected method is adequately supported
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not operate a separate general-purpose Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to the regimes applicable in certain offshore financial centers. Nevertheless, substance is material under corporate income tax, transfer pricing, permanent-establishment, withholding, anti-avoidance, beneficial-ownership, and deductibility rules. The JV should maintain Taiwan personnel, premises, decision-making, operational controls, trial-management capability, risk management, books, and contemporaneous evidence proportionate to the CRO functions it claims to perform. Artificial arrangements, conduit payments, circular cash flows, and contracts inconsistent with actual conduct may be recharacterized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing CRO revenue, issuing false invoices, overstating trial expenses, fabricating subcontractor charges, omitting foreign-source or Taiwan-source income, or using sham cost allocations to reduce taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional tax, interest, administrative penalties, tax assessment, possible prohibition from claiming unsupported deductions, and criminal prosecution. Intentional tax evasion may carry imprisonment of up to five years and a criminal fine that may reach NT$10 million under the Tax Collection Act, subject to the applicable offense and court determination.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible persons may face criminal liability, civil restitution, tax-related personal sanctions where statutory conditions are met, asset seizure, and disqualification consequences. Travel restrictions may arise during criminal or enforcement proceedings; imprisonment is possible for aggravated or intentional offenses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using fictitious vendors, backdated invoices, fabricated investigator-site costs, sham consulting agreements, duplicate expense claims, or false accounting records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax penalties, denial of deductions, recovery of tax credits, criminal liability under tax, accounting, commercial, or criminal law, and potential forfeiture of proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors, managers, accountants, and employees may be prosecuted personally. Civil damages, restitution, asset preservation, travel restrictions, and imprisonment may apply depending on the conduct and loss amount.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging the Taiwan JV excessive management fees, royalties, financing costs, or data-platform fees; assigning Taiwan functions without corresponding remuneration; or shifting CRO profits to the mainland parent without commercial evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authority adjustment to arm's-length income, denial of deductions, withholding-tax reassessment, interest, penalties, and documentation penalties where applicable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil liability to the company or shareholders for intentional or negligent misconduct. Criminal exposure generally requires additional fraudulent, false-document, or evasion conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to withhold on nonresident dividends, royalties, interest, service fees, or other Taiwan-source payments; applying treaty relief without a valid residence certificate; or remitting gross amounts without tax settlement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unpaid withholding tax from the payer, interest, withholding penalties, and possible restrictions on tax clearance or remittance processing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The withholding agent's responsible person may face personal administrative or criminal exposure where the failure is intentional, falsified, or part of tax evasion. Civil recovery claims and enforcement measures may follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Permanent establishment and Taiwan-source income risk
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the JV as an undisclosed dependent agent, fixed place of business, or operational platform for a foreign enterprise while reporting only a limited service margin or no Taiwan income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of Taiwan-source income, corporate income tax, withholding tax, penalties, interest, and possible permanent-establishment compliance obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face liability for knowingly implementing an artificial structure or submitting false filings. Criminal consequences depend on proof of intentional evasion or falsification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Managing regulated clinical trials, handling human-subject data, operating trial sites, or performing regulated medical or pharmaceutical functions without required approvals, licenses, ethics review, or competent-authority authorization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines, suspension or revocation of approvals, corrective orders, trial suspension, invalidation of data, civil claims, and criminal sanctions under applicable pharmaceutical, medical, personal-data, and human-subject protection laws.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible officers may face personal criminal, civil, and administrative liability, including professional disqualification, travel restrictions during investigation, and imprisonment for serious unlawful conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Personal data and clinical-trial confidentiality breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Transferring patient, genetic, health, investigator, or trial-subject data to mainland China or another jurisdiction without lawful basis, consent, security controls, contractual safeguards, or required regulatory approval.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines, corrective orders, data-processing suspension, contractual damages, compensation to affected persons, and criminal liability for serious unlawful disclosure or misuse.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible individuals may face personal criminal and civil exposure. Directors may be liable for inadequate governance, failure to implement security controls, or knowingly authorizing unlawful transfers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained milestone payments, disguising shareholder funding as service revenue, using nominee shareholders, failing to identify the ultimate beneficial owner, or processing payments through opaque intermediaries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customer due-diligence deficiencies, reporting failures, account restrictions, administrative fines, transaction suspension, asset freezing, and money-laundering prosecution where knowledge or wilful blindness is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may face personal fines, civil liability, criminal prosecution, asset forfeiture, travel restrictions, and imprisonment for laundering or facilitating illicit proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Taiwan JV with no personnel, premises, decision-making, or operational capability while routing dividends, royalties, financing, or clinical-trial payments through it solely to obtain tax or regulatory benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, tax reassessment, withholding-tax recovery, anti-avoidance adjustment, penalties, and potential criminal investigation if documents or filings are false.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face breach-of-duty claims, restitution, asset-preservation measures, travel restrictions, and criminal sanctions where the structure involves fraud, false documents, or intentional tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Remitting profits through undocumented service fees, false loans, excessive royalties, unauthorized capital movements, related-party netting, or offshore payment accounts without required Taiwan banking and tax compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Foreign-exchange penalties, tax reassessment, withholding-tax liability, repayment orders, bank reporting, account restrictions, and criminal sanctions for serious or fraudulent violations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors and officers may face personal fines, civil restitution, asset seizure, travel restrictions, and imprisonment where illegal remittance or concealment is intentional.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends without distributable earnings, before required financial approval, while insolvent, or without satisfying withholding-tax and statutory reserve requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of improperly distributed amounts, director liability for company losses, shareholder repayment obligations, corporate-law sanctions, and tax reassessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly liable for restitution and damages and may face criminal liability where the distribution involves false accounts, insolvency abuse, or intentional creditor prejudice.
